Implementation Details. Consistent with previous works (Tan et al., 2024; Jiang and Ye, 2023), we utilize the CLIP ViT-B/16 model as our backbone. Following IRRA (Jiang and Ye, 2023),we incorporate a randomly initialized multimodal interaction encoder to facilitate masked token prediction. Our implementation processes $3 8 4 \times 1 2 8$ resolution images with a maximum length of $N = 7 7$ text sequences. We employ Adam (Kingma, 2014) as the optimizer, initialized with a learning rate of $1 e - 4$ and a weight decay of $4 e - 5$ . The parameters $\beta _ { 1 }$ and $\beta _ { 2 }$ are set to 0.9 and 0.999, respectively. The temperature parameter $\tau$ in SDM loss is set to 0.02. We train GA-DMS for 30 epochs with a batch size of 512 on 8 NVIDIA A100 (80G) GPUs. For generating synthetic templates and captions, we utilize Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (Yang et al.. 2024a), Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5- VL-32B-Instruct (Bai et al., 2025). Additionally, vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023) is leveraged to accelerate large-scale inference. Please refer to the Appendix A.1 for more detailed hyperparameters. Evaluation. Following previous works (Tan et al., 2024; Qin et al., 2024), we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of our method across three challenging text-to-image person retrieval datasets: CUHKPEDES (Li et al., 2017), ICFG-PEDES (Ding et al., with ALBEF(Li et al.,2021) backbone:
